text: Sections 1, 2, 7, 9 and 10 are read per service: the single recovery_svc login of version 4 becomes the 19 logins rwb_<short with _>, each with grants on its own schema only, and rwb_source_data is the only login that holds SELECT on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views.
why: Version 4 predates the 19-service split and names one login; Architecture v5 slide 29 and Rules v1 R4 name one login per service, and the document must describe the target state.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 29 and 41; Rules v1 R4; ADR-014; split_plan.json legacy RWB-E1-001 and RWB-E1-069
applied_in: sections 1, 2, 7, 9, 10 and the realignment table, rows 1 and 2
confirm: The ACE DBA confirms the grant set of each of the 19 logins at the wave 1 build.
impact: Every story that touches the database builds against a per-service login; no story builds against recovery_svc.

text: The authorise contract is the four operations that Architecture v5 slide 14 names (POST /authorise with role, scope and DoA; GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits; /masking-policies), owned by P4 rwb-access, with the request and response shapes left to RWB-P4-E1037-CON and its fake in RWB-PLT-E1037-CON.
why: The operations are named but no shape exists in the API Specification or the Ownership Map, and DP-08 needs a published contract before any service can build against it.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 14 and 41; Rules v1 DP-08; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet
applied_in: sections 1, 2, 4, 4.1 and 10 and the realignment table, row 5
confirm: P4 rwb-access publishes the OpenAPI contract and the platform publishes the fake before the wave 1 build starts.
impact: The 19 services code against the contract and the fake, never against a private copy; a shape change is a contract change.

text: Masking is applied twice and both controls stay: rwb-source-data masks in v_ace_customer and v_ace_contact and in its contract, and every service re-applies the masking_rule rows of rwb-access at its own API before the response leaves.
why: Architecture v5 slide 39 and slide 35 give different single answers, and the source document makes the API mask the control; with 19 services the two together are the only reading that loses no control.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 35 and 39; v4 section 5; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet, masking_rule to P4
applied_in: sections 1, 4, 5 and 9 and the realignment table, row 6
confirm: Compliance confirms that masking in the owning service at the API is the primary PDPA control and that the view mask is a second control.
impact: Two stories per service can own a mask; the compliance test 'Masking' checks the API result, not the view.

text: SY-CASEWF is the identity of P3 rwb-case only; another service starts a child workflow through a signal to the CaseWorkflow instead of holding SY-CASEWF. SY-RULES is one role held by each of the 19 service identities inside its own embedded runtime.
why: Version 4 gives the rights to single roles but does not say which service identities hold them once every service has its own workload identity and its own embedded Drools runtime.
read: v4 sections 4.1 and 7.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 35 and 41; Temporal and Drools design L2 and L4; ADR-017
applied_in: sections 4.2 and 7.1 and the realignment table, rows 8 and 9
confirm: The platform and P3 rwb-case confirm the mapping in the authorizer plugin configuration of the rwb-recovery namespace.
impact: No service except P3 needs a Temporal right to start a case workflow; the plugin refuses any other start with MSG-P4-002.

text: The access log is a table in rwb_access named access_log, owned by P4 rwb-access, with the append-only rule of version 4 section 8 and the read path GET /admin/access-log.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name the object and the map gives the read operation to P4, but the Tables sheet has no row for it, so the document needs a stated reading.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet, GET /admin/access-log
confirm: The Ownership Map gains an access_log row at its next revision.
impact: The P4 database story creates the table; no other service writes to it.

text: The view conformance test of RWB-E1-069 sits with the P1 rwb-source-data slice, because that is the only login that holds the view grant; the P4 slice keeps the role, scope, masking and DoA checks, and each service runs its own boundary test on cross-schema references.
why: The legacy story is one and the split plan gives it four slices across two services, so the pipeline check needs one owner.
read: v4 sections 7 and 10; split_plan.json legacy RWB-E1-069; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29
confirm: P1 and P4 agree the slice boundary in the wave 1 build.
impact: The build fails on a public table grant in the P1 pipeline and on a cross-schema reference in every service pipeline.

text: A partner user is created and ended by the administrator of S9 rwb-partner, and the roles it holds are P4 rwb-access role rows granted by the P4 role owner; the partner gateway in the DMZ authenticates it under FAPI 2.0.
why: Partner users moved to S9 while the role model stayed in P4, and version 4 names one role owner for a single role model.
read: v4 section 6; Ownership Map v1 Rulings sheet, partner_user to S9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 35 and 41
confirm: S9 and P4 confirm the split before the partner portal opens.
impact: Two owners act on one partner user, and both actions land in the access log.

text: The codec server and the codec keys are platform components of RWB-PLT-E2038: one key per namespace, the previous key kept so old histories decode, and the rotation run under the key policy of SCB IT security.
why: Version 4 gives the codec server one key and no owner; Architecture v5 holds the keys per namespace and gives each namespace its own certificates and keys.
read: v4 sections 5, 7 and 7.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 35 and slide 41 notes
confirm: The platform confirms the key hierarchy and the rotation window in the wave 0 build.
impact: A decode after a rotation still works for old histories; only RW-SECADM can decode, inside a break-glass session.

text: The document is issued as Draft. No approval is recorded for this version, so the overlay of the D-RCV-60 run is applied and the status is written as Draft until a later verification loop approves it.
why: AGENTS.md rule 9 and the run overlay: a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and work continues in Draft.
read: AGENTS.md rules 1 to 14; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R8.1
applied_in: the metadata table of the document
confirm: The programme records the approval of version 5 in the document control record.
impact: No downstream stage treats this version as approved.

text: Dates are kept as the source writes them: version 4 is dated 16 November 2026 and stays visible in the metadata and change-log rows, version 5 is dated 22 November 2026, and the one forward date in the document (DL43, by 21 November 2026) is kept character for character and read as tentative under U7.
why: Rule 10 and U7: dates are copied unchanged and are never raised as a gap, and any release date is marked tentative rather than moved.
read: v4 metadata table, change-log row and section 11 row DL43; Rules v1 R1 U7
applied_in: the metadata table, the change log and section 11
confirm: The programme office refreshes the dates when the plan is rebaselined.
impact: No date in the document is moved or dropped.

text: Every owner named in version 5 is the service code of the Microservice Ownership Map v1 and _work/msr/plan/ownership.json: P4 for role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict, delegation_limit and the access log; P7 for rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and the central decision ledger; S9 for partner and partner_user; P5 for retention; P1 for rwb_source_data and the views; PLT for the guard library, the codec server and the Temporal Web UI.
why: The work package requires the Ownership Map for every owner, and the story masters are the lowest source in the precedence order.
read: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (Services, Tables, Endpoints, Rulings); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
confirm: The owner of each row is confirmed in the service contract catalogue.
impact: No table, workflow or operation in the document has two owners.

text: The 19 service codes, names, waves, schemas, REST bases, topics and task queues in version 5 are those of the Ownership Map v1 Services sheet and Architecture v5 slide 41, and the task queue of a service is rwb-<short> in namespace rwb-recovery.
why: Rules v1 R4 fixes the naming and the map fixes the 19 rows; the document must not restate them from memory.
read: Ownership Map v1 Services sheet (19 rows); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29, 41 and 44; Rules v1 R4
confirm: The naming library RWB-PLT-E1047-CON encodes the same rules.
impact: A service added or renamed later changes the map first and this document second.

text: The new decisions used in version 5 are the ones allocated in _work/msr/plan/ids.json: ADR-013 to ADR-023 as cited, and DL44 to DL49 in section 11. No new ADR or DL number was allocated by this work package.
why: Rules v1 R8.4 names ADR-013 to ADR-023 and Decision Log rows DL44 to DL49, and the overlay forbids inventing an identifier.
confirm: The architecture decision record set records ADR-013 to ADR-023 with the text of R8.4.
impact: A reader can trace each change of version 5 to an allocated decision.
